newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.S. official studies smuggling in Panama.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official studies smuggling in Panama.

text.p: U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Jonathan Winer investigated potential weapons, drugs and illegal immigrant smuggling routes on Monday in Panama's remote Darien jungle, U.S. embassy officials said.
Winer spent Monday in a helicopter over the Darien jungle which borders Colombia and has long been a haven for smugglers, said an embassy official who asked not to be identified.

"It was a fact-finding mission to see if we can assist in any way to combat these problems," the source said. "All the drugs, arms and illegal immigrants coming through destabilises the country which we don't want," said the official.
The U.S. government agreed to give Panama six helicopters to help combat drug-rafficking.
The helicopters, to come from U.S. military reserves, will be used by Panamanian police to destroy drug crops in Darien.
The source said Winer's visit was separate from one by Defence Secretary William Perry, scheduled to visit Panama Saturday before heading to Argentina.
